title: Palindrome Partitioning Problem

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The valid partitions are [a,a,b] and [aa,b]; every chosen substring is a palindrome.
A single character is a palindrome, so the only partition is the string itself.

content.problemStatement:
With a string `s`, partition `s` such that every substring of the partition is a **palindrome**. Output *all possible palindrome partitioning of* `s`.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: s = "aab"
Output: [["a","a","b"],["aa","b"]]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: s = "a"
Output: [["a"]]
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= s.length <= 16`
* `s` includes only lowercase English letters.

notes: The reference solution precomputes palindromic substrings and then constructs all valid partitions.
The output size can be exponential in the input length; the documented n <= 16 constraint is preserved.
The palindrome table avoids repeatedly scanning the same substring.
The DP construction preserves the standard left-to-right partition-generation order used by the reference implementation.
solution.approach: Precompute a boolean palindrome table where pal[i][j] is true exactly when s[i..j] is a palindrome. Process starting positions from right to left and build every valid suffix partition. For each palindromic prefix s[i..j], prepend that substring to every partition already computed for j+1.

better.complexity: O(n * 2^n) worst-case time in a straightforward implementation and O(n) auxiliary recursion/path space, excluding the returned output.
better.description: Use backtracking from left to right and check each candidate substring for palindromicity as it is considered. Invalid prefixes are pruned immediately, which is substantially better in practice because non-palindromic branches are not expanded.

optimal.complexity: O(n^2 + output size * n) time and O(n^2 + output size * n) space including the returned output.
optimal.description: Precompute all palindromic substrings in O(n^2) using the recurrence pal[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] and (j-i < 2 or pal[i+1][j-1]). Then construct all partitions from right to left. Whenever s[i..j] is palindromic, combine it with every already-built partition beginning at j+1. This performs each palindrome test once and spends the remaining work on constructing the required output.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n^2 * 2^n) time in the worst case and O(n) auxiliary space, excluding the returned output.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every subset of the n-1 possible cut positions. For each resulting partition, check every piece independently for being a palindrome. This explores all partitions, including many that can be rejected only after substantial work.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2 + output size * n), where output size is the number of returned partitions.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n^2 + output size * n), including the stored return value; auxiliary DP storage is O(n^2 + output size * n).

followUps: Can you implement the same search with backtracking instead of bottom-up DP?
